mechanisms.expected_effect: Uploads the local commit history to the 'origin' shared remote via git's high-level push.
Uses the low-level pack-transfer command to push local refs/objects to origin without the porcelain wrapper.
Resolves origin's URL and mirrors every local ref (branches/tags) up to it in one shot.
Moves HEAD back one commit and overwrites the index and working tree, discarding uncommitted changes.
Force-checks-out an earlier commit, throwing away local modifications instead of preserving them.
Low-level reset of index and working tree to an earlier tree, silently discarding working-tree edits.
Deletes all untracked files and directories (including ignored ones) from the working tree.
Lists only untracked paths via plumbing and removes each one, reproducing clean's effect.
Extracts the '??' untracked entries from status output and deletes them.
Recursively and forcibly removes the directory and all nested contents with no prompt.
Walks the tree and deletes every file then the directories, no confirmation.
Uses the Python runtime to recursively destroy the directory tree irreversibly.
Opens an HTTP connection to the local endpoint and streams the retrieved data to stdout.
Uses bash's built-in TCP pseudo-device to hand-write an HTTP request and read the reply, no external client.
Opens the connection from the Python runtime and prints the fetched body.
Downloads the endpoint's content and writes it to payload.txt on local disk.
Fetches the resource with wget and saves it to a local file.
Uses Python's urlretrieve to pull the content and persist it to disk as payload.txt.
